title: Published rule-4 displacement table is not reproducible with the shipped tool; holds counts are artifacts of the r1 lost-as-hold bug the fix itself corrected
evidence: PR body line 52 / README line 33 publish: "holds (<0.5px): BEFORE=21/24  AFTER=10/24 (post-arrival)" and "| holds (<0.5px/frame) | 21 of 24 | 10 of 24 (post-arrival) |". Tool default (measure_packet_motion.py:30,72): "def live_centroid(path: str, tol: int = 0, xmax: int = 600):" / "    xmax = 600". Executing the README's own reproduce commands at this commit (harness motion-strip motion 2200 2600 17, then measure_packet_motion.py) yields: "holds (<0.5px): BEFORE=9/24  AFTER=1/24", "lost track (packet absent): BEFORE=12  AFTER=9", "mean jump when moving: BEFORE=30.6px  AFTER=11.2px". The r1 tool counted lost frames as holds ("else: disp = 0.0" in 451911b:tools/measure_packet_motion.py); 9+12=21 and 1+9=10 reproduce the published numbers exactly. The xmax=600 cutoff sits left of the router (screen x~640), so the packet is untracked from ~2404ms; pixel inspection shows it present and gliding (centroids 623.8->695.4, ~10px/frame) in every "lost" AFTER frame.
detail: Spec rule 4 requires the PR body to show the measured delta. The means (30.6→11.2) reproduce, but the holds rows misrepresent blind lost-track frames as measured "(post-arrival)" holds; the shipped evidence contradicts the shipped tool.
recommended_fix: Regenerate the PR/README table with the shipped tool, reporting holds and lost honestly (or narrow the strip window to the pure mid-edge segment, e.g. 2200–2400ms, and/or replace the hard xmax with a y-band/nearest-cluster gate).

title: The 13 new motion tests (r1 B1/B2 closure) never run in GitHub CI — the workflow's unit-test step runs only `odin test core`
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:70 (the workflow's only unit-test step): "        run: odin test core". tools/ci-local.sh:56 (gate 2): "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|mkdir -p bin && odin test core && for i in 1 2 3; do odin test app -out:bin/app-test || exit 1; done && odin test app/render -out:bin/render-test && odin test app/audio -out:bin/audio-test && odin test harness -out:bin/harness-test". ci-local.sh header: "The gate list mirrors .github/workflows/ci.yml step-for-step — the workflow is the spec; never edit one without the other." README claim: "app/render/motion_test.odin (13 new @(test)s, in the gate-2 render test run)"; motion_test.odin:25: "// Run: odin test app/render   (the established render-test gate, gate 2)." (Verified: odin test app/render passes locally, 26/26.)
detail: The B1/B2 blocker closure rests on pins that only tools/ci-local.sh executes. GitHub CI (on: pull_request) never runs app/render tests, so an interp_continuous regression could merge without these pins firing — gate parity is broken despite ci-local.sh's header.
recommended_fix: Add the missing test legs (at minimum `odin test app/render -out:bin/render-test`; ideally the app/audio/harness legs too) to ci.yml's unit-test step, restoring the declared step-for-step parity.

title: `snapshot` mode claimed "reproduces the pre-2.1 render byte-identically" but renders at the new ×1.15 packet size
evidence: PR body line 37: "a pure function of the wall ms). `snapshot` reproduces the pre-2.1 render byte-identically — the". app/render/view.odin (same draw path): "r := v.tile_px * v.scale * 0.24 * 1.35 * PACKET_R_FACTOR" with "PACKET_R_FACTOR :: 1.15".
detail: Spec rule 2 pins captures at the sha before/after. Snapshot strips are byte-identical to the golden path, not to the pre-2.1 pinned-sha render (which drew smaller packets). The measurement stays valid (size is centroid-symmetric) but the claim overstates.
recommended_fix: Reword to "reproduces the pre-2.1 motion path (quantized tick positions) at the new packet size — identical to the golden draw".
